Salesforce and Microsoft Announce Copilotforce, Bringing Salesforce Customer Context and Sales Workflows to Microsoft Copilot
November 17, 2026
7 min read
New integrations bring Salesforce customer context and sales workflows into Microsoft Copilot, enable real-time CRM collaboration in Microsoft Teams, and connect Salesforce Data 360 with Microsoft Fabric through bidirectional zero-copy data access. Accenture is serving as design and implementation partner along with being customer zero, deploying the integrations in its own global sales organization.
SAN FRANCISCO & REDMOND, Wash. – November 17, 2026
. Today at Microsoft Ignite, Salesforce and Microsoft announced Copilotforce, a partnership bringing Salesforce to Microsoft’s expansive enterprise productivity ecosystem, alongside new integrations across Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams, and Microsoft Fabric. The collaboration extends Salesforce customer context, AI capabilities, and sales workflows into one of the largest enterprise software environments, bringing Salesforce closer to where employees already work.
With Salesforce in Microsoft Copilot, sellers will be able to access Salesforce customer context, analyze opportunities, prepare for meetings, prioritize opportunities, and take CRM actions informed by Teams conversations, Outlook emails, and shared documents. Separately, bidirectional
zero-copy capabilities
connect Salesforce
Data 360
and Microsoft Fabric without duplicating datasets, allowing organizations to query Fabric data natively within Data 360 and securely share Data 360 intelligence into Fabric.
These capabilities build on
Sales Cloud
in Teams, which brings Salesforce CRM insights and workflows into Microsoft Teams, introduced at Dreamforce and currently in pilot. Together, the integrations will allow sellers to prep for meetings in Copilot or Teams, or update supported opportunity details in Teams.
“Through Copilotforce, we’re bringing Salesforce to the largest surface in enterprise software today, embedding trusted Salesforce context and intelligent sales workflows directly where sellers work. By bringing together the #1 CRM with the #1 productivity surface, we’re transforming AI from a standalone tool into a powerful driver of productivity, smarter decisions, and customer success.”
–
Miguel Milano, President, Chief Operating Officer, Salesforce
“AI is only as powerful as the data and context that grounds it. Bringing Salesforce customer data and sales skills together with the work context delivered by Work IQ in Microsoft Copilot allows our joint customers to unlock actionable insights across their core business applications. Copilotforce will give sales teams the intelligence they need to make faster, higher-confidence decisions while maintaining the governance and trust enterprises demand.”
–
Judson Althoff, CEO, Microsoft Commercial Business
AI context where employees already work
Powered by
AIforce
, the live interface layer that brings Salesforce capabilities into external AI environments, Salesforce in Microsoft Copilot will bring Sales Cloud workflows into the tools sellers already use. Sellers will be able to prepare for meetings, review opportunities, and take supported sales actions using Salesforce customer context.
Salesforce in Microsoft Copilot:
Will enable sales and revenue teams to ask natural-language questions and receive grounded, actionable outputs; will also enable users to take Salesforce actions directly within Copilot. Work IQ, the intelligence layer that powers Copilot, synthesizes Salesforce insights with relevant relationships and content from Teams meetings, Outlook emails, and shared documents across SharePoint and OneDrive. Key daily sales workflows will include:
Customer Meeting Preparation:
Combine account history and meeting transcripts into a single executive brief, saving hours of prep time and eliminating app-switching.
Deal-Health Analysis:
Surface hidden deal risks and customer sentiment, enabling sellers to focus on the right actions before deals stall.
Pipeline Review & Action Plans:
Turn complex pipeline data into ready-to-execute close plans directly inside Word and PowerPoint, slashing administrative overhead.
Salesforce in Teams:
Building on the pilot demonstrated at Dreamforce 2026, the Sales Cloud in Teams app will bring rich business context and real-time insights directly where over 400M active users already chat and collaborate. Sellers will be able to act on those insights with Agentforce Coworker, with updates automatically syncing back to Salesforce, and it brings the same Salesforce permissions and governance coordinating the right Agentforce agents, and turns the chat into action. Sellers will gain a real-time view of pipeline and quota progress, receive active deal notifications, and access AI-driven briefing materials. Interactive adaptive cards will enable sellers to update supported opportunity details, with changes saved back to Salesforce, and share secure records in deal rooms to align cross-functional teams without tool-switching.
Enterprise-grade governance and source-level permissions
Enterprise AI requires strict
data protection
and
governance
controls. Salesforce in Microsoft Copilot operates through authenticated user access, preserving the granular permissions, sharing rules, and audit trails established in both environments.
Customer data remains protected at every boundary: Salesforce controls data access and governs supported business actions, while Microsoft ensures communications and documents adhere to existing enterprise compliance policies. Supported writeback actions to the CRM require explicit user confirmation and respect existing validation rules, helping ensure customer records remain governed and auditable.
Related
Informatica from Salesforce brings Trusted Enterprise Data into Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Foundry, and Microsoft Fabric to Accelerate AI & Analytics
7 min read
Why We Post-Trained Our Own Reasoning Model
6 min read
Access enterprise context without migration or duplication
AI models
and enterprise workflows are only as effective as the data and context they can reach. Salesforce and Microsoft are delivering bidirectional Zero Copy integration between Salesforce Data 360 and Microsoft Fabric, allowing organizations to harmonize and activate data across platforms and turn customer, operational, and financial data into trusted context for AI, without maintaining duplicate datasets or running brittle
ETL pipelines
.
Data Federation:
Joint customers can now query and analyze supported Microsoft Fabric OneLake data directly within Salesforce Data 360, leaving the source data in Fabric. This native Zero Copy connection brings Salesforce and Microsoft Fabric data together, turning it into enterprise-wide context across Salesforce experiences: Sales and service teams get a richer view of each customer, marketers build segments from the combined data, analysts explore it in
Tableau
, and
Agentforce
uses it to answer questions and complete tasks.
Salesforce Data 360 Data Sharing:
Organizations will be able to securely share curated Salesforce Data 360 customer context and intelligence into Microsoft OneLake. Enterprise data science and business intelligence teams will be able to analyze customer trends alongside enterprise datasets, helping business leaders make decisions with a more complete picture of their customers and operations. That combined context will support custom analytics, reporting, and enterprise AI workloads without maintaining duplicate datasets, helping teams make more informed decisions grounded in trusted customer context.
Trusted enterprise data for Microsoft AI and analytics ecosystem
Enterprise AI
and analytics systems demand trusted data, rich business contexts, and governed access. Through an expanded collaboration with Microsoft, Informatica helps customers make confident decisions, simplify AI development, and understand the data powering their AI and Analytics workloads. The new
Informatica Plugin for Copilot
empowers business users to discover relevant data, address data quality issues, and verify the authoritativeness and reliability of the underlying data using natural-language queries. Enhanced Foundry capabilities enable developers to build high quality and governed AI agents with minimal custom integration. Additionally, expanded Fabric scanning helps data and AI teams trace data lineage and analyze downstream impacts on analytics.
Accenture: validating real-world value
Accenture is collaborating with Salesforce and Microsoft as the design and implementation partner to shape the enterprise solution architecture and bring deep expertise in delivering business outcomes across 13 industries globally.
Having scaled Microsoft Copilot to more than 740,000 people and as one of the largest Salesforce users globally with 55,000 active users, Accenture is serving as Customer Zero for this solution, deploying and validating the integrations within its own global sales organization and sharing learnings to help customers reach value sooner. Through real-world deployment, the companies are helping clients turn investments they have already made in Salesforce and Microsoft into a better way to sell, driving faster growth and getting deals back on track.
“As a Global Partner of the Year for both Salesforce and Microsoft and one of their top customers, we are uniquely positioned to bring our expertise to help design and implement Copilotforce so that our clients can quickly get more value from their technology investments. The combined strengths of our three companies will reinvent sales with AI, giving sellers more time with customers while trusted intelligence and agents work alongside them in the tools they already use. We are also excited to serve as customer zero for Copilotforce.”
– Julie Sweet, Chair and CEO, Accenture
Availability Roadmap:
Salesforce in Microsoft Copilot – Public Preview (Beta)
Integration enabling sales teams to ask natural-language questions and receive grounded, actionable outputs. Available in our AgentExchange and the Microsoft Copilot plugin directory.
Salesforce in Teams
–
Pilot
The Sales Cloud in Teams app brings rich business context and real-time insights to enable sellers to view pipeline progress. While Agentforce Coworker allows sellers to delegate work and take action directly within Teams without leaving the teams.
Data Federation – Generally Available
Allows joint customers to natively query and analyze Microsoft Fabric OneLake data directly within Salesforce Data 360 without leaving the source data in Fabric or maintaining duplicate datasets. Available on our
Data 360 Developer Guide
.
Salesforce Data 360 Data Sharing – Public Preview, Beta
Allows organizations to securely share curated Salesforce Data 360 context and intelligence into Microsoft OneLake to support custom analytics, reporting, and enterprise AI workloads. Available on our
Data 360 Help Page
.

Informatica & Microsoft: Trusted Enterprise Data - Salesforce
Skip to Content
Skip to Footer
0%
Salesforce Partners
Informatica from Salesforce brings Trusted Enterprise Data into Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Foundry, and Microsoft Fabric to Accelerate AI & Analytics
November 17, 2026
7 min read
Expanded Microsoft collaboration brings Informatica’s enterprise data intelligence directly into Microsoft Copilot for business users and Microsoft Foundry for AI developers, while strengthening trusted analytics across Microsoft Fabric.
Announcement Highlights
Bringing Trusted Enterprise Data to Microsoft Copilot and Teams:
New integration extends Informatica’s enterprise data intelligence into Copilot & Teams, helping business users and executives access authoritative business definitions, data quality, governance, and lineage insights through natural-language experiences.
Powering Governed AI Agents in Microsoft Foundry:
Expanded integration with Informatica Headless introduces new Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based governance, identity, and administrative capabilities, enabling developers to build agents grounded in trusted data.
Expanding Trusted Governance for Microsoft Fabric:
Enhanced scanning and lineage capabilities now include notebooks and pipelines, providing greater visibility into how data moves and transforms across analytics workloads.
Expanding Deployment Choice on Microsoft Azure:
A new U.S. East Coast Azure point of delivery expands deployment choice for enterprises with regional data residency and compliance considerations.
Informatica
, a leader in AI-powered enterprise cloud data management, today announced an expanded collaboration with Microsoft at Microsoft Ignite 2026.
The collaboration introduces a Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Teams integration and expanded
data governance
capabilities for Microsoft Foundry and Microsoft Fabric. As enterprises move from AI experiments to agents performing business-critical work, those agents need more than access to data. They need to understand business definitions, identify authoritative sources, assess data quality, and operate within access policies.
According to Deloitte’s 2026
State of AI in the Enterprise
report
, 85% of organizations expect to customize
AI agents
for their business needs, but only 21% of organizations planning agentic AI deployments report having mature agent governance models.
Informatica addresses this challenge by bringing the intelligence embedded within its AI-ready Data Platform that includes enterprise business glossaries, metadata, lineage, data quality, master data, and governance directly into the AI experiences enterprises are adopting.
“The next frontier of enterprise AI isn’t simply giving every employee an intelligent assistant or every developer the ability to build agents. It’s ensuring that those assistants and agents understand the business they’re operating in.
With Informatica and Microsoft’s AI and Analytics experiences, we’re bringing trusted enterprise data directly to where people ask questions, make decisions, and build intelligent systems. Business users can benefit from the same authoritative data intelligence that developers use to build governed AI agents.
We’re making enterprise data management more accessible, more intelligent, and more relevant to every person and every agent across the organization.”
—
Savinay Berry, EVP & General Manager, Data Management, Salesforce
Bringing trusted enterprise data to Copilot
Informatica’s new integration with Copilot is designed to bridge that gap by making enterprise data intelligence accessible within the conversational AI experiences employees use to get work done. Through
Informatica Headless
capabilities, Copilot experiences are enriched with enterprise context drawn from Informatica’s data catalog, business glossary, metadata, lineage, quality indicators, and governance services.
This means business professionals can move beyond asking what information exists to understanding what that information actually means, where it originated, how trustworthy it is, and how it should be interpreted. Imagine a marketing manager using Copilot to create a campaign that targets a segment of customers for a new feature launch. To develop an effective campaign, the marketing manager needs to identify the most relevant and authoritative datasets, assess their quality, understand the data lineage and provenance, and ensure compliance with access control for sensitive information, including Personally Identifiable Information (PII). By bringing together these critical elements of enterprise data context through Informatica MCPs into the Copilot experience, the marketing manager (business user), can confidently design, execute and optimize campaigns using trusted, governed and AI-ready data.
Copilot brings AI to the business user. Informatica brings the enterprise’s trusted data intelligence to Copilot.
Extending Foundry with governed enterprise data for AI agents
While Copilot makes trusted context more accessible to business users, Foundry provides developers with the tools to build and deploy AI agents that can reason and act across enterprise systems.
Building on the general availability of Informatica Headless MCP servers in Foundry announced at Informatica World 2026, the expanded integration introduces new and updated governance, identity, and administrative capabilities.
These enhancements expand access to Informatica’s data management capabilities through standardized MCP interfaces and enable enterprise AI developers to:
Ground AI agents in trusted business data: Give agents access to authoritative definitions, quality indicators, and lineage so they can better understand and interpret enterprise information.
Govern agent access and actions: Apply identity, access, and administrative controls that help keep agent activity within established enterprise policies.
Enhanced governance and auditability: Administrative capabilities help customers control and trace agent interactions with enterprise data management services.
Accelerate enterprise AI development: Enable Foundry developers to discover and use Informatica’s data management capabilities through standardized MCP interfaces rather than building custom integrations.
Drive multicloud enterprise context: Informatica enables Foundry agents to benefit from governed data intelligence spanning systems and environments beyond Microsoft Azure.
By expanding the availability of Informatica’s MCP services across Azure-based IDMC points of delivery worldwide, more organizations can incorporate trusted enterprise data into Foundry applications and agents.
Deepening trusted analytics across Fabric
As enterprises increasingly adopt Fabric to unify their analytics environments, understanding how data moves and changes across complex workloads has become essential to maintaining trust. Informatica is extending its Fabric scanning capabilities to include notebooks and data pipelines, expanding governance visibility beyond data at rest to the orchestration and transformation processes that shape enterprise information.
The enhanced scanners provide broader lineage visibility across data movement and transformation workflows, including multistep pipeline orchestrations. These innovations help customers:
Expand end-to-end data lineage by tracing data movement and transformation across Fabric notebooks and pipelines.
Strengthen governance and impact analysis: Better understand dependencies and the implications of changes across Fabric environments.
Simplify administration: Manage Fabric scanning services through a consolidated interface, reducing operational complexity.
Enrich enterprise context for AI with lineage, provenance, and governance intelligence that can inform downstream AI experiences.
Deliver more reliable analytics and AI: Provide data engineers, analysts, and AI developers with greater confidence in the provenance, quality, and meaning of the data they consume.
As Informatica extends governance and lineage visibility across Fabric, the resulting metadata and trust signals enrich the enterprise context made available to AI agents through Copilot and Foundry.
“
As AI becomes part of everyday work, organizations need intelligent experiences that understand the business context behind their information. Microsoft Copilot helps people work more effectively, Microsoft Foundry enables developers to build powerful AI agents, and Microsoft Fabric serves as a primary data source fueling these experiences. Microsoft IQ brings these capabilities together with a shared intelligence layer that connects data and business context to help AI understand how an organization works. Our expanded collaboration with Informatica brings authoritative data definitions, quality, lineage, and governance into these experiences. By combining Microsoft’s AI innovation with Informatica’s enterprise data management, we’re helping customers make AI more relevant, more trustworthy, and easier to scale
.”
— Yitzhak Kessleman, Corporate Vice President, Microsoft IQ, Microsoft
Expanding Informatica’s Azure footprint to support enterprise choice
Informatica is also expanding its geographic footprint on Azure, with a new U.S. East Coast point of delivery. The new deployment option is designed for enterprises seeking to align cloud architecture, data residency preferences, and procurement requirements with U.S. East Coast–based infrastructure.
The new Azure pod offers Informatica’s broad portfolio of cloud data management services, including data integration, data governance, data quality, master data management, and agentic data management capabilities. Customers will also be able to benefit from advanced serverless integration capabilities available as an Azure Native ISV Service.
Customers can apply 100% of the pre-tax amount of Informatica offers, purchased through Microsoft Marketplace toward their Microsoft Azure Consumption Commitment (MACC), subject to Microsoft’s eligibility requirements.
“
Integrating Informatica with Microsoft Foundry and Fabric is helping Wescom Financial close the gap between raw data and real AI readiness. We now have the contextual, trusted data layer our teams need to deploy AI with confidence — and that’s accelerating how quickly we can turn insight into action
.” —
Desigan Reddi, Vice President of Enterprise Architecture and Innovation, Wescom Financial

items.title: New Data: Holiday Shoppers Will Rely on Agents. Retailers Must Be Ready.
items.content:
The AI-First Holiday: Shoppers Let Agents Do the Legwork - Salesforce
Skip to Content
Skip to Footer
0%
Commerce
New Data: Holiday Shoppers Will Rely on Agents. Retailers Must Be Ready.
A Salesforce survey shows that holiday shoppers are using AI agents for research and advice — almost 20% of shoppers now say that AI is their first stop on the way to the store — but most aren’t ready to let AI click Buy Now.
November 12, 2026
4 min read
Somewhere on Cyber Monday, a shopper will ask AI to find the best price on a stand mixer for their sister-in-law, check whether the reviews recommend it, and flag anything that won’t arrive before December 20. Then they’ll close the app and buy it themselves.
For millions of people in 2026, holiday shopping starts with AI. Salesforce proprietary research shows that AI is projected to drive $75.8 billion in Cyber Week spending, up 13% from 2025. AI-driven recommendations are expected to influence more than 1 in 5 holiday orders. Traffic flowing to ecommerce sites from AI tools has more than doubled, up 104% year over year.
And, according to a new Salesforce Consumer Shopping survey of more than 2,500 shoppers in the U.S., the U.K., Canada, and Australia, almost 20% of shoppers now say that AI is their first stop on the way to the store, and 74% trust the recommendations it gives them. AI is also reshaping which brands get noticed: 30% of AI shoppers say these tools frequently introduce them to brands they didn’t know. And it can stop a sale as easily as start one. Eleven percent of shoppers say they’d skip a purchase if an AI assistant advised against it.
“AI is no longer a niche tool just for tech-savvy shoppers,” said Caila Schwartz, Head of Agentic Commerce Shopper Insights at Salesforce. “Everyday shoppers are asking AI what to buy, where to buy it, and whether it’s worth the money before they ever land on a retailer’s site.”
Personal agents are catching on, but shoppers aren’t handing over their wallets yet
Shoppers are adopting personal AI agents to compare products and check reviews, but for now, they’re treating these agents like advisors rather than buyers.
Thirty-one percent of consumers have tried a personal AI agent. Meta Muse is the most widely adopted, used by 12% of consumers surveyed. It’s also the most recognized, followed by Grok Bot.
Among people who use them, agents are becoming a daily habit: 28% of personal agent users give their agent tasks multiple times a day.
The most common shopping tasks people use their agents for are to compare prices, analyze product specifications and reviews for sizing quirks or technical differences and product discovery like brainstorming gifts based on criteria.
Open Image Modal
Image Modal
However, shoppers are not quite ready to let agents check out for them. That might change as trust grows.
Only 19% of personal agent users have deployed their agents at checkout.
Shoppers who do let agents buy are setting firm limits. Just 9% of personal agent users give their agents unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card just for their agent.
About three-quarters of shoppers (73%) aren’t comfortable giving a personal AI agent their payment information to make purchases and 49% are not interested in agents browsing or buying on their behalf at all. The biggest obstacles are unwanted sharing of purchase history or personal data and accidental or unwanted charges.
Open Image Modal
Image Modal
Agents pay off for retailers, but shoppers won’t forgive many mistakes
Retailers that offer their own
shopper agents
are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The catch is that shoppers have very little patience for AI that gets things wrong.
Shoppers who arrive through AI referrals are more than two times as likely to convert as typical ecommerce shoppers.
Thirty-nine percent of shoppers have used a brand’s shopper agent on an ecommerce site. Eighty percent of them reported a good experience, and 75% of that group felt more loyal to the brand afterward.
Shoppers who engage with a brand shopper agent spend more, with an 8% higher average order value, and buy 23% more items than the average order.
Brands that deploy AI shopping agents see seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.
Open Image Modal
Image Modal
However, trust in AI is fragile and brands need to nurture it carefully.
Most shoppers will abandon an AI assistant after just two or three mistakes, and when AI makes a bad recommendation, 32% of shoppers blame the AI.
Twenty-seven percent of personal AI agent users say their agent has bought something that was too expensive, 22% have had their agent blocked from completing a purchase, and only 32% report no major errors at all.
Open Image Modal
Image Modal
The bottom line: Be ready for agents, and earn consumers’ trust
As more shoppers send personal agents to compare prices and read reviews for them, retailers will need to handle that nonhuman traffic without slowing their sites or degrading the experience for human shoppers. Their own shopper agents and product data will also need to be ready for the questions those personal agents ask.
“My advice before Cyber Week is simple: Be the brand that AI can find and humans can trust,” Schwartz said. “Shoppers are starting with AI this season, so make sure your product data is accurate, your prices and inventory are current, and your own agent is ready to answer the hard questions.”
For now, the shopper buying a stand mixer is still the one entering their card number. The retailers that earn their trust this season will be in the best position when they’re ready to hand that over too.
